result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.constraint()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate Burt's constraint for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14301-L14472){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.constraint(weights=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Burt's constraint measures the extent to which ego's contacts are redundant, that is, connected to each other. Higher constraint indicates fewer structural holes and less brokerage opportunity. Lower constraint indicates a network position with more non-redundant contacts, offering greater access to diverse information and control benefits. The constraint of node i's ego network is: `C_i = Σ_j (p_ij + Σ_q p_iq × p_qj)²` where `p_ij` are proportional tie strengths: `p_ij = (a_ij + a_ji) / Σ_k (a_ik + a_ki)` and `a_ij` are elements of the adjacency matrix (edge weights). Time complexity: `O(V × D²)` where `D` is average degree Space complexity: `O(V)` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of edge attribute to use as weights. If `None`, uses edge weight field. If weights don't exist, treats all edges equally. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store constraint values. If `None`, uses `constraint` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to constraint values. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float | None] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`, a dictionary mapping node IDs to constraint values is returned. Returns `None` for isolated nodes (undefined constraint). If `return_dict=` is `False`, returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Interpretation**: - **High constraint** (approaching 1.0): Ego's contacts are highly interconnected. Limited brokerage opportunities, high closure. - **Low constraint** (approaching 0.0): Ego's contacts are disconnected. Many structural holes, high brokerage potential. **Structural holes** occur when ego's contacts are not connected to each other, providing opportunities for: - information brokerage (access to diverse information) - control benefits (mediating between disconnected groups) - innovation (combining ideas from separate clusters) **Use cases**: - social capital analysis: who has advantageous network positions? - innovation research: individuals spanning structural holes - organizational networks: identifying key boundary spanners - entrepreneurship: access to diverse resources and information **Undefined values**: Isolated nodes have no ego network and return `None`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate and store constraint values: ::: {#44de9483 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Simple network with a broker (B) g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") # Broker .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("B", "D") # Note: C and D are not connected .constraint() # Stores as 'constraint' attribute ) # Access values by node ID b_id = g.get_id_from_label("B") a_id = g.get_id_from_label("A") constraints = g.constraint(return_dict=True) # Low constraint value for broker B (more structural holes) constraints[b_id] # High constraint value for node A (fewer structural holes) constraints[a_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: Analyze structural holes: ::: {#66bc3153 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Compare dense vs. sparse ego networks g = ec.Graph() for i in range(6): g.add_node(label=str(i)) # Node 0: connects to 1,2 which are connected (no structural hole) g.add_edge(source="0", target="1") g.add_edge(source="0", target="2") g.add_edge(source="1", target="2") # Node 3: connects to 4,5 which are NOT connected (structural hole) g.add_edge(source="3", target="4") g.add_edge(source="3", target="5") # Note: 4 and 5 are not connected constraints = g.constraint(return_dict=True) node_0_id = g.get_id_from_label("0") node_3_id = g.get_id_from_label("3") # Higher constraint for node 0 (dense ego network) constraints[node_0_id] # Lower constraint for node 3 (sparse ego network with structural hole) constraints[node_3_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.5 ``` ::: ::: Weighted networks: ::: {#a91b25e1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=5.0) .add_edge("A", "C", weight=1.0) .add_edge("B", "C", weight=3.0) ) # Strong tie to B dominates A's network constraints = g.constraint(return_dict=True) # Returns dict mapping node IDs to constraint values constraints ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 1.0277777777777775, 3: 2.6180555555555554, 2: 0.703125} ``` ::: :::
